body: Nalanda Gedige is an ancient archaeological site located in Sri Lanka, near the town of Matale, in the central part of the island. It is believed to be a Hindu temple complex, and it is renowned for its unique architectural style, which is a fusion of South Indian Dravidian and traditional Sinhalese designs.The term "Gedige" refers to a building or structure, and Nalanda Gedige is often described as a temple or shrine that dates back to the 8th to 10th centuries. Its origins and purpose are still subjects of debate among historians and archaeologists, but it is thought to have served religious or ceremonial functions, possibly dedicated to Hindu deities or used for Buddhist rituals.The temple's design is notable for its intricate stone carvings, including depictions of gods, animals, and mythical creatures, showcasing the craftsmanship of the era. The site has been partially restored and is a popular tourist attraction, offering insights into Sri Lanka's rich cultural and religious heritage.

body: I’m not sure why not more people stop here because it’s well worth the visit. Perhaps because it’s free, people don’t think it’s worthwhile. However, it’s beautiful complete stone temple, which used to mark the centre of Sri Lanka. It has Buddhist and Hindu elements, making it unique. Use one of the guides and remember to tip him, he will take whatever you give him so 500-600 SLD was very much appreciated in 2019.
title: Well worth the visit

body: One of the ancient monuments in sri lanka. Stories says that this is the center of Sri Lanka. Place based on buddhism but some cultural behaviours had effected the building. It has been re constructed in the same place in 1980s as it was founded around 40 feets deep and it was going to flooded by the Bowatenna Reservoir. You can get more info from the office located at the entrance. Lovely and calm place to visit.
title: The Heritage of Sri Lanka

body: this monastery is a less travelled historic icon by tourists. an entire collection of stone buildings carved out of rock. an ancient engineering marvel. this place is mostly visited by local Buddhists.

body: Just 1km distance from Mathale - Dambulla road. entrance is free. This building was created 8-10 AD. This been used by buddhist, but the building architecture is hindu. this temple was dismantle and rebuild on the retaining wall of bowatenna tank in 1980s. Around the walls of the temple many hindu and buddhist designs can identify. Inside there is a beautiful load buddha's stratue. Left side of the nalanda gedige there is a stupa. Near the entrance gate you can see small museum.
title: Unique structure with buddhist & Hindu mixed

body: It has been relocated and is a good visit to experience ancient way of building. Assume it is made out of entirely stones and rock and no cement equivalent paste used. A beautiful lake adjoins the building. No tickets, free entrance. Nice tranquil area.

body: This stop on along our trip from Dambulla to Kandy was well worth it. There were no tourists and it was so quiet. You walk a little ways from the car park along a long tree-lined path with the reservoir on both sides. Eventually the path opens up and this little temple appears. Its in great shape--as is the Buddha shrine within. Bring something to feed the dogs who look particularly neglected. The land contains a huge tree of enlightenment.
title: Well preserved temple off the beaten path

body: It's known as the center point of the country and located in between Dambulla and Kandy route. A must see place if you are seriously in to cultural tourism. title: Must see cultural site

body: Another location unknown to our taxi driver that we wanted to visit. A beautiful atmospheric ruin half Hindu half Buddhist. A small basic museum was close by explaining some of the history, then a short walk to the ruin. We were approached by a caretaker who wanted to explain the features to us which made it all more informative for a small tip. Very calm relaxing place and well worth a look if you have time.

body: We stopped for 45 min at this dite on the way from Trincomalee (via Dambulla) to Kandy. This is one of the most well-preserved sites we saw in Sri Lanka. Not large but really beautiful with all carvings in stone still visible! It is only 10min off the main road between Kandy & Dambulla.
title: Worth a stop on the way from or to Kandy

body: One of the more intricately done historical places in Sri Lanka is the Nalanda Gedige. Historically a gedige is part of a monastic building, specifically an image-house or pilimage. Nalanda is situated in the Matale area, some 29 kilometers off Aluvihare. The latter is well-known for having been the site where the Theravada Buddhist teachings were compiled in written form after a period of over four centuries to that date. To this day, this compilation is known as the Tripitaka. The Nalanda Gedige does contain images in it, to wit a standing Buddha statue and some others, not nearly as well-preserved.
title: Nalanda Gedige

body: It was baffling to see how the generations before us constructed this temple by identifying the center of Sri Lanka. Entrance is free so it's a must visit site. Don't forget to switch on Google maps and see for yourself as to how accurate this location is.

body: It's a convenient distance between Dambulla and Kandy so a decent rest stop. It's a beautiful little temple, admission is free, and it's also in a very peaceful setting. No crowds of tourists or people selling tat, just a car park and the temple.Well worth a quick stop - there's not a whole lot to see so you'll probably only be around 20 minutes, but it's a good place to stretch your legs.
title: Great little find

body: This temple was recently cut up into pieces and moved to higher ground, where it is now, otherwise it would have been at the bottom of the reservoir that surrounds it. A beautiful, very old temple, this is worth a small detour to see. Set in a beautiful park, this is one of the older temples in the area.
title: Nice Old Temple

body: A great example of South Indian style architecture in Sri Lanka The building was moved to its current location to save its loss in the waters of the nearby reservoir
title: Peaceful historical site

body: It took me about 40 minutes from Matale in a car.Lovely.Its not that big but its really worth the visit.Dont rush - wander round and take in the buildings and the small information centre and museum.The fact that its the very centre of Sri Lanka makes it feel more special.Don't miss the opportunity to go down to the lake. You have to drive or walk round a bit further on the road to get to it as its not accessible from the actual temple sight.You only need and hour or so to do the temple and the lake.... but its well worth it.Just watch out for the Spice Gardens near by. They invite you in for a free tour and they try to sell you stuff at ridiculously high prices. Nothing to do with the temple but worth mentioning.

body: An ancient complete stone temple located at what is said to be the center point of the island, with well known Pallava architecture of Mahabalirupam in South India. In 1980 during construction of the Mahaveli river project and relocated to its current raised terrace 8m above its original location.
title: worth to visit

body: It was just 01km away from main A9 road close to Nalanda town.One of the few places you can visit without paying entrance charges.It considered as center of Sri Lanka.Build in South Indian architecture and it housed Buddha's images.It can be considered as one of the best preserved stone monument.

body: Historically important place. It says that this is the right middle of Sri Lanka. Not too much locals visit this place.

body: This was described as the absolute centre point of the island of Sri Lanka though when you go there very little suggests this to be the case. What you do find is a Buddhist temple which was rescued from the rising waters of the Nalandia Gedige reservoir by building a platform onto which the temple was moved stone by stone.The highlight was what the guide described as “Giant Squirrels” and he wasn’t kidding, these things were the size of terriers!

body: So lovely place, it' free, we had no one with us, and it's really lovel. All the historg is in the routard guide, so you don't even need someone to visit it. If you're as lucky as us, you'll enjoy the sun on stupla and temple... rellly lovely place
title: Picturesque

body: On the benefit of the Elders in our area the executive committee of the Elders Society of Grama Niladari Division of Gangodawila East, Nugegoda is arranging an excursion to places of ancient archeological interest. In November 2016 we arranged an excursion to Kandy Dalada Maligawa, Matale Nalanda Gedige, Ragiri Dambulu Viharaya and Robodagalla Stone Statue of Lord Buddha. Nalanda Gedege is one of the sight we visited and most of our elder members really like it. According to the history the structure of Nalanda Gedege was created between 8th and 10th century AD. This Gedege is completely made out of stones and it is a mixture of Tamil and Sinhala culture. Nalada Gedege was hidden in the jungle for a long period of time and British Archaeologist Mr. Bell found it in 1893. In 1980 it was dismantled and reconstructed at a different place because newly created Bowatenna Tank threatened to flood the shrine. Everyone who visit Sri Lanka should visit this wonderful place.
title: Excursion of Elders Society of Gangodawila, Nugegoda, Sri Lanka

body: Too many reasons to visit this. Very scenic place in the middle of no where away from all the touristy crowd. So you can soak into the atmosphere in peace. Though it is a single temple, it is beautiful and worth the diversion. Ask your driver\guide to take here as it is usually not included in the tourist circuits.There is no hiking or steps involved and it takes hardly half hour for the entire visit plus no entrance fees! There are not many visitors and as other reviewers have said it was moved, but apparently used to be underground. body: One of the oldest buildings in SL is found on the road south from Dambulla to Matale. If you're passing you will be well rewarded if you stop by. We were the only people there and I doubt there are many visitors. It's free to see and is a small temple consisting of an image house, a stupa and a Bodhi tree. The architecture is part Buddhist and part Hindu. There's a small museum also. The setting is tranquil and delightful although not the original as the whole thing was moved when the adjacent reservoir was formed otherwise you would have needed scuba gear to see it. Well worth 30 mins of your time

body: The hybrid of Hindu and Tantric Buddhist influences is throughout this structure. Situated in this forest with serene landscape, this is a must see. Please take your shoes off and walk within the temple itself. The voice of serenity is only divine magic. Truly lovely and a gem.
title: Heart of Sri Lankan culture and history at its best!

body: A nice mixture of both religious and ancient architecture. It's not your typical dome temple, different. Has very unique archaeological features not seen in most temples. If you have time during your transit from Kandy to dambulla, try to visit.

body: Built in 7-8 AD. According to the archeological department this monument related to the Mahayana chapter and architecture is combined with Buddhist and hindu characteristics. body: This is a stone building which is very old situated in between Matale and Dambulla cities. For me, this is as good as visiting a spice garden because you get some time off from the car and have a walk while you see things. Most tourists are not families with this place or the operators do not promote this. Anyway if you are on your own, have a visit, There is a reservoir near by and known as this temple was relocated few hundred of meters due to the construction of that reservoir. The place is very calm and quiet and have a pleasant climate.The stone building has a Buddha statue inside and outside you may notice many carvings, Some says those are "The carving of two men in a sexual position with a lion" but you will hardly notice it because those are really small.I recommend this place to any families where nature is proffered with ancient touch.

body: Not so far from Matale town. There was good architecture. It is ancient Hindu temple.This temple built between 8th to 10th centuries. Nalanda is 20km north to aluwihare temple. I came from A9 route from Kandy then one kilometer distance from A9 route from “nalanda” junction. I saw very old carvings on wall. There was stupa near “Nalanda Gedige”.
title: One of good architectural temple of 8th 10th centuries.

body: Nalanda Gedige is small but has a charm of its own. It is an ancient complete stone building of Hindhu temple and the main deity was Sri Vishnu. It is located in Nalanda in the Matale district little off the main road of Dambulla Matale. This ancient Hindu Temple was constructed in between 7th to 10th century with the dravidian architecture with pallawa style (Koil) and then used by Buddhists also. The location is considered as the centre of Sri Lanka.The address of the Nalanda Gedige is Gedige Rd, Nalanda and it is open in all the 24 hours. It is managed by the archaeological department of Sri Lanka.Little forest cover near and around it, is noted. You hear the sounds of insects and birds. Two and half sides of the stone temple is covered by water of the Nalanda tank/ lake. The water in it is used for irrigating agriculture. It has nice views onto the tank. There is a notice to say not to go down to the tank from there, meaning not to bathe in it. It is a quiet, peaceful and lonely place and one could stay for a while for relaxation. The time I went a tourist bus just took off and arrived a bus of school children. Schools are obligatory to take children on a picnic during the first term as specified by the department of Education for them to get to know important places of Sri Lanka. It also gives them enjoyment and be off from routine schedule. You can feel the breeze and the place is cooling even during hot sun as the place is covered by canopy of the trees around the place. It’s a beautiful place and couples would call it as romantic also. The Indian Kama Sutra carvings are also found. There was a carving of two men in sexual position with an animal suspected to be a lion.It is managed by the Archeological department of Sri Lanka presently. They only elevated 9 meters from the level of the tank and rebuilt the temple stone by stone. The place is the centre of Sri Lanka and for marking it, this temple must have been built. Inside the temple is beautiful too. There is no entrance fee. The entrance path has a stone carved rectangular structure and the path leading to it is decorated with stone carvings.The architecture is mainly from South India but some mix up of Sinhala ones are also found. No history of the Nalanda Gedige is known. However it is believed that the Hindhu Temple was built in 7 -8 centuries.
title: Nalada Gedige the Centre of Sri Lanaka, Archeological Department Rebuilt it Stone By Stone.

body: This temple is only small, and we were the only people there, and that's what made it so worth going. You walk to it through the jungle, just listening to natural sounds in the moist heat, and look around the heavy stones, hundreds of years old.
title: Atmospheric

body: I planned a journey to Nalanda Gedige today. The trip took 5 hours to see a simple site. Here's how; leave hotel 6:30, cane to bus station, make sure driver knows where to drop me off, (RS 40) 50” later drop off, caned 1km to the site, looked around & shot photos, walked to tank/lake to see some birds, caned back to road, wait for “the right” bus on the side of the road (RS 43) journey back at bus station 50” later & walk back to hotel. 5 hours. There isn't much there, but IF you go, don't forget (unless you're on a tour....bus & your moments are being timed) to go out the back & have a look at the tank/lake where you may see some birds. It's free too!
title: IF you are passing by.........stop by, man.

body: This temple is easy to miss, but worth your time. We were literally the only people there for most of our time there. Our driver suggested it on our way back to Kandy from Sigiriya. We were grateful for this stop.

body: This is an interesting and unique place due to it's architecture and the fact that not much is known about it's history. It has a curious mix of Sinhalese and Hindu architecture and even an out of place carving of two men in a sexual position with a lion. What makes it more interesting is that the Sri Lankan archaeological department took this apart and rebuilt it 'brick by brick' on ground raised 9 metres to prevent it from going under the lake that was built in the recent times.If you are after big monuments such as in ancient cities this is not the place. But for an unusual and interesting place with beautiful views due to the nearby manmade lake, this is a must see place.
title: Less visited place

body: Supposedly the geographic centre of Sri Lanka. A quick detour, in case you are on the Dambulla - Matale Road, to view a unique temple (which is fairly weather beaten!) that has both Buddhist and Hindu elements. The views of the artificial lake are a bonus. Go with low expectations as the Gedige is simply plain in contrast to the awesome monuments of Anuradhapura or Polonnaruwa. body: Visiting before the hideous 'cleaning' of rocks that the archeological department is going to undertake. The structure depicts both Hindu and Buddhist carvings making it a likely structure by an Indian invader. What's unusual is that a stone carving of a 'karma sutra' is also part of the structure. The only one in Sri Lanka I have been told. The Buddha statue inside the building is beautiful. I enjoyed the visit here. The architecture and style is unique to Sri Lanka and this is meant to be the Centre of the island.

body: The place has a historic temple which displays features of ancient Indian architecture. The place the temple was situated has been shifted slightly and reassembled due to construction work of Bowathenna lake.

body: A little quiet temple all to ourselves. Worth the detour and a good spot if you want to stop for nice cool breeze and place to eat your packed breakfast or lunch in the shade with good views and no monkeys!

body: being directly on the main route between Kandy and Sigiriya, this temple was a welcome break from the drive and turned out be an amazing piece of history. Granted, the temple was moved here in the 80s to save it from the hydroelectric company's flooding of the valley, but this unusual temple was preserved meticulously and is an amazing example of purely south indian design seen in many Hindu Shrines, but oddly enough there is no historical mention to this place being anything but a Buddhist place of worship since its founding somewhere in the 7th - 12th centuries.Though you may have to pay an entrance of 500 rupees at times, I would highly recommend stopping by here if you have the chance

body: Very cool temple, with an unusual mix of Hindu and Buddhist iconography, but the grounds keeper thinks it's pretty funny to show off the carvings of tantric sex. I think these are unusual artifact in Sri Lanka, so I see why it's important to point out, but as two women, it made us a bit uncomfortable the way he was talking about it. body: If you are visiting Polonnaruwa or Dambulla, you must visit nalanda gedige! Unless you are using a prado or something similar, you better go to Dambulla and take the main road, because road goes through Diyabeduma is under constructions and from the looks of those huge breakdowns, it would take months to complete the road! This is the perfect center of the country and is been restored perfectly due to the built of the lake. One of the other coolest thing about this place is the weather contrast you will definitely notice--To the left side of the nalanda gedige you will feel the coolness and to the right it is hot!In Polonnaruwa kingdom period, kings got married to princesses from India, who belong to hindu religion. For the convenience for both king and queen to be able to embrace their religious rituals, they have build both temples in one building. You can see one side of the building's with Lord Buddha & buddhist symbols and on the opposite side of it hindu gods & symbols. Take a closer look at each carving, and you will find at least an hour fascinating yourself with so many different symbols and it's architectural differences. You will find a pig, a lion, a man-woman-horse, a lord buddha statue, a rare lord ganesh's statue and so many other interesting ones.There are 3 historians from archeology department, who are more than happy to share their knowledge about this place and it's history! There is a museum with some more historical details and you can check it out for free :)
title: Right middle of Sri Lanka -- where two religions meet!

body: A place worth of dropping by on the way to Kandy or Dambulla ton inspect a rare blend of Buddhist and Hindu architecture... The Nalanda Gedige proudly stands in the center of Sri Lanka (wonder how they mapped it) as a symbol of Ethnic Harmony Sri Lanka had thousands of years back. Though it's an archaeological wonder, it seems to be off the beaten path - or it was when we visited. It was a nice change from the other, heavily-trafficked tourist destinations.

Nalanda gedige is situated about 1Km from Naula town. ( Naula is in between Matale and Dambulla). I have visited there on an evening and it was a nice place. body: Nalanda Gedige is one of a number of remarkable archaeological sites in Sri Lanka that receive few tourists through no limitations of their own. The reasons for this anomaly are various. Sometimes it has to do with geography and ease of access, although this is not the case with Nalanda. Often, however, it is a case of the beaten tourist track prevailing over good sense. Gedige is an image house - is strongly recommended, because it exhibits a composite style of architecture unique in Sri Lanka, and an extraordinary fusion of Hinduism and Buddhism. To cap it all, this remarkable shrine occupies an extremely picturesque - if not original - location.Nalanda Gedige is “one of those fortunate places that have no history.” The surprising lack of knowledge regarding this shrine, and why it was located at Nalanda thwarts those who wish to delve into its past. Even estimates of its date of construction vary from the 7th to 11th centuries AD. It still retains its unique appearance of mixing features of Hindu architecture with that of Buddhist designs. On the other hand, Nalanda Gedige features several Tantric Buddhist carvings which were damaged through time. Roland Raven-Hart wrote that the structure makes use of Buddhist ground plan with Hindu vestibules.
title: Center of Srilanka - By Serndip Traveller

body: Nalanda gedige is located 24km away from Dambulla towards to matale.It was constructed using stones in between 8th -10th Century AD as a Hindu temple.But later period artists made more stone carved Buddha images here.so, these days we consider this as a Buddhist image house and Hindu architecture still can be seen.Curious stone carved image is located just outside the stone image house.You can see two men in a sexual position with a lion.this image is unique and can't anywhere in Sri Lanka .

body: There was nobody else there, that was the big plus. So quiet and next to a lake.Small temple and we are near "temple overload" but this was a worthwhile stop.Look for the naughty brick design on the side.
title: A short worthwhile visit

body: It's amazing to imagine how our ancestors calculate the exact spot of the center of Sri lanka. Although it was relocated but on the same spot much higher than the original spot when rapid Mahaweli development was taking place in 1980's. It has Sri lanka and indian mixture of architecture. Mostly Pallawa of south Indian is visible. Ruind pagoda is nearby. So Buddhist and Hindu worshiping has taken place here. Was a meeting place of ancient armies in the central hills. One special sculpture attract my attention. Only here you can find that type of art in Sri lanka. In Lakshman Temple, Khajuraho India you can see pleanty. Just 01km from main road gets you here. So far entrance tickets not required. But if you wish you can drop a little donation. Staff friendly enough to guide you. Please pay amall amount as tip. Try to visit this place.
title: Center of the Geological Sri lanka
Worth a detour
body: A small Hindu temple sitting by a Buddhist tomb in a lovely setting, next to a lake and with views of the mountains in the distance. Few people seem to make it here, and the peace and quiet in such surroundings is a nice respite from the usual hustle and bustle of Sri Lanka. There is no charge, but you may be accompanied by the janitor, who speaks some English. He may well show you the museum at the end of your visit, close the door behind you and ask for a donation. Fair enough, but you have been warned...

title: Visiting Nalanda Gedige
body: It is well maintained and there is no littering . Obvious the Dept of archaeology has done a good job on planning conservation in this site this site. Signage could however improve for foreign tourists especially.

title: A hidden gem, a highlight of our trip!
body: One of the genuine "Indiana Jones" momments of our trip.A small sign on the main Kandy-Dambulla street shows you the way to the Nalanda Gedige.A strange, ancient temple but conserved in great shape. Inside the temple Vishnu and Ganesh statues coexist with Budha's. There's a bodhi tree and if you search the reliefs you can find some very interesting scenes, although quite worn with time...The place is quiet, we were alone for most of the time, and quite unusual for Sri Lanka, there's no ticket to be payed!The lake views around the temple are beautiful, and you might as well walk to the lakeshore to get some photos but beware of the serpents!

title: Peaceful and ancient
body: On your way through Matale heading toward the Cultural Triangle sites of Dambula and Siguria is a beautiful devale, or roofed temple dating from 8th - 10th centuries. The site is very atmospheric as there are few visitors and it is off the road about .5 km. The temple is well preserved and shows signs of Mahayana Buddhism -- especially tantric. See if you can spot the image from the Kama Sutra on the outside of the temple. Inside are some fine sculptures. Although the visit will be brief, it is certainly worth a stop.Follow the Kandy Dambula Road out of Matale and turn right at the Nalada Hospital. Follow the dirt track to the end and the temple is there-- free of charge. A plug for a good driver: Lucky operates out of Kandy and has a Tata Nano or a tuktuk - 077 650 8265. He is not a scammer, in my experience -- friendly and patient.

title: Delightful
body: There is something very fine and calming about this simple temple, and although you're unlikely to spend more than 20 minutes there, it may well remain in your memory as one of the better sites in Sri Lanka. The tranquil setting and the building's humble dimensions - not to mention the good state of preservation and the mind boggling lack of any entry fee (long may this last!) - combine to make this a very worthwhile stop indeed.

title: Center of Sri Lanka
body: At the geographical center of Sri Lanka this small temple without entrance fee is worth the visit for people who are more interested in history. If you go for the symbol which is known, you should know it is the only symbol.

title: Little gem
